tasks.title: First channel
tasks.statement:
Create mpsc::channel(4). From a spawned task send 1, 2, 3 (and close the channel by dropping the sender). In main read with while let Some(v) = rx.recv().await and print the values, and after the loop print "end".

Expected output:
`1`
`2`
`3`
`end`
tasks.hint: The Sender moves into the task via async move; once it is dropped, recv() returns None.

tasks.title: Several producers
tasks.statement:
Spawn three tasks, each sending its own number 0, 1, 2 through a shared channel (tx.clone()). Collect all values, sort them and print the vector with {:?}.

Expected output:
[0, 1, 2]
tasks.hint: Drop the original tx, otherwise recv() will never finish.

tasks.title: Closed channel
tasks.statement:
Create a channel mpsc::channel::<u32>(1), drop the sender and print rx.recv().await with {:?}.

Expected output:
None
tasks.hint: A closed and empty channel returns None.

tasks.title: No receiver
tasks.statement:
Create a channel, drop the receiver and send a value. Print "send failed: true" if send returned an error.

Expected output:
`send failed: true`
tasks.hint: tx.send(1).await.is_err() after drop(rx).

tasks.title: try_send and overflow
tasks.statement:
A channel of capacity 2. Call try_send three times: for successful ones print "ok", for an overflow (TrySendError::Full) print "full".

Expected output:
`ok`
`ok`
`full`
tasks.hint: use tokio::sync::mpsc::error::TrySendError; match tx.try_send(i) { Ok(()) => .., Err(TrySendError::Full(_)) => .., _ => .. }

tasks.title: capacity
tasks.statement:
A channel of capacity 3. Print tx.capacity() before sending and after one send (a send without waiting: try_send).

Expected output:
3
2
tasks.hint: capacity() is how much free room is left.

tasks.title: reserve and permit
tasks.statement:
A channel of capacity 1. Reserve a slot with tx.reserve().await, send 5 through the permit (permit.send(5)) and print rx.recv().await with {:?}.

Expected output:
Some(5)
tasks.hint: let permit = tx.reserve().await.unwrap(); permit.send(5);

tasks.title: Unbounded channel
tasks.statement:
Using mpsc::unbounded_channel send the numbers from 0 to 999 (send without .await), drop the sender and print "sum: …" (add up everything received).

Expected output:
`sum: 499500`
tasks.hint: tx.send(i).unwrap(); then drop(tx) and while let Some(v) = rx.recv().await.

tasks.title: Order from one sender
tasks.statement:
One task sends 0, 1, 2, 3, 4; the receiver collects the values into a vector. Print the vector with {:?}: the order is preserved.

Expected output:
[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
tasks.hint: mpsc preserves the order of messages from one sender.

tasks.title: oneshot: a task's result
tasks.statement:
Spawn a task that sends 21 * 2 over a oneshot channel. Wait for the value with rx.await and print it.

Expected output:
42
tasks.hint: let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel(); tx.send(..); rx.await.unwrap().

tasks.title: Request with a reply
tasks.statement:
Spawn a worker task: it receives pairs (u32, oneshot::Sender<u32>) over mpsc and replies with the square of the number. Send a request (5, reply_tx) and print the reply.

Expected output:
25
tasks.hint: Worker: while let Some((n, reply)) = rx.recv().await { reply.send(n * n).ok(); }

tasks.title: The oneshot sender is gone
tasks.statement:
Create a oneshot channel, drop the sender without sending and print the error from rx.await with {} (the Display of RecvError).

Expected output:
channel closed
tasks.hint: if let Err(e) = rx.await { println!("{}", e); }

tasks.title: try_recv on oneshot
tasks.statement:
Create a oneshot channel. Print rx.try_recv() with {:?} before sending, then send 7 and print try_recv() again.

Expected output:
Err(Empty)
Ok(7)
tasks.hint: The Receiver must be mutable: let (tx, mut rx) = …

tasks.title: Broadcast to two receivers
tasks.statement:
Create broadcast::channel(8) and two subscribers (tx.subscribe()). Send «a» and «b». Each subscriber reads two messages. Print «r1: a b» and «r2: a b».

Expected output:
r1: a b
r2: a b
tasks.hint: Each subscriber gets a copy of every message.

tasks.title: A lagging subscriber
tasks.statement:
broadcast::channel(2): send 1, 2, 3, 4 without reading. Then read: on a Lagged(n) error print "skipped n", print values as they are, until the end of the buffer (3 reads).

Expected output:
`skipped 2`
`3`
`4`
tasks.hint: use tokio::sync::broadcast::error::RecvError; Err(RecvError::Lagged(n)) => ..

tasks.title: Late subscription
tasks.statement:
Create a broadcast channel, send «old», then subscribe (subscribe) and print late.try_recv() with {:?}: the subscriber will not see the old message.

Expected output:
Err(Empty)
tasks.hint: Keep the first receiver (let (tx, _rx)), otherwise send returns an error.

tasks.title: watch: the current value
tasks.statement:
Create watch::channel(0), send 5 and print *rx.borrow().

Expected output:
5
tasks.hint: tx.send(5).unwrap(); *rx.borrow().

tasks.title: watch: waiting for changes
tasks.statement:
A task updates the value of a watch channel: 1, 2, 3 with a 40 ms pause between updates and then finishes. In main wait for rx.changed().await in a loop and print the new value.

Expected output:
1
2
3
tasks.hint: while rx.changed().await.is_ok() { println!("{}", *rx.borrow()); }

tasks.title: A counter under a Mutex
tasks.statement:
Ten tasks increment a shared counter Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<u32>> by 1. Wait for all of them and print the value.

Expected output:
10
tasks.hint: *m.lock().await += 1;

tasks.title: A lock across await
tasks.statement:
Two tasks take the same tokio::sync::Mutex and hold the guard during a 50 ms sleep. Print "sequentially: true" if all the work took at least 90 ms.

Expected output:
`sequentially: true`
tasks.hint: let _g = m.lock().await; sleep(..).await; — the guard lives until the end of the block.

tasks.title: Fix it: std Mutex across await
tasks.statement:
The program does not compile: the std::sync::Mutex guard lives across .await inside spawn. Fix it by shortening its lifetime (increment the counter in a separate block before the sleep). Expected: "counter: 1".

Expected output:
`counter: 1`
tasks.hint: Wrap let mut g … *g += 1; in a separate pair of braces before .await — the guard will be dropped earlier.

tasks.title: RwLock: a writer and readers
tasks.statement:
Put a number into Arc<RwLock<u32>>: first write 10, then spawn three reading tasks, each returning what it read. Add up the results and print "sum: …".

Expected output:
`sum: 30`
tasks.hint: *lock.write().await = 10; let v = *lock.read().await;

tasks.title: Limiting parallelism
tasks.statement:
A semaphore with 2 permits, six tasks: each takes a permit, increments a counter of simultaneously running tasks (AtomicUsize), updates the maximum, sleeps 50 ms and decrements the counter. Print "maximum at once: 2".

Expected output:
`maximum at once: 2`
tasks.hint: cur.fetch_add(1) + 1; max.fetch_max(now); then cur.fetch_sub(1).

tasks.title: acquire_owned
tasks.statement:
A semaphore Arc::new(Semaphore::new(3)): spawn three tasks, each gets a permit through acquire_owned().await (it moves into the task) and sleeps 30 ms. After all of them, print available_permits().

Expected output:
3
tasks.hint: sem.clone().acquire_owned().await.unwrap() — a permit with ownership.

tasks.title: try_acquire
tasks.statement:
A semaphore with one permit. The first try_acquire succeeds (print "ok"), and while the permit is held, the second one fails (print "busy").

Expected output:
`ok`
`busy`
tasks.hint: let p = sem.try_acquire(); … sem.try_acquire().is_err()

tasks.title: Notify: waking a task
tasks.statement:
A task waits on notify.notified().await and then prints "woke up". The main task prints "waking" and calls notify_one(), then waits for the task to finish.

Expected output:
`waking`
`woke up`
tasks.hint: Notify in an Arc; the waiting task is a spawn; wake with notify.notify_one().

tasks.title: Notify: the remembered permit
tasks.statement:
Call notify_one() before waiting, then notified().await — it must not block. Print "does not block".

Expected output:
`does not block`
tasks.hint: Notify remembers one permit if nobody is waiting.

tasks.title: Barrier
tasks.statement:
Barrier::new(3) and three tasks: each increments a shared AtomicUsize counter, then waits at the barrier and after it checks that the counter equals 3. Print "all see 3: true".

Expected output:
`all see 3: true`
tasks.hint: barrier.wait().await; after the barrier all three increments are already done.

tasks.title: A counter actor
tasks.statement:
Write an actor: a task owns a counter and accepts commands enum Cmd { Add(u32), Get(oneshot::Sender<u32>) } over mpsc. Send Add(3), Add(3), Add(4), then Get and print the reply.

Expected output:
10
tasks.hint: Actor: let mut total = 0; while let Some(cmd) = rx.recv().await { match cmd { .. } }

tasks.title: Worker pool
tasks.statement:
Three workers take jobs from a shared channel (the receiver in Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<Receiver<u32>>>), compute the square and send the result to a results channel. Send jobs 1…9, close the jobs channel and print "sum of squares: …".

Expected output:
`sum of squares: 285`
tasks.hint: Worker: let job = { let mut g = rx.lock().await; g.recv().await }; None — leave the loop.
